type: Captioned recording of actual app operation; no synthesized personal voice

captions.title: ReachLab · Engineering within reach
captions.text: A local robotics workbench for learning without owning a robot. Design an arm, train a model, and test predictions.

captions.title: 1 · Explore the mechanics
captions.text: Two joint angles determine the tip position. Link lengths define the reachable region. This is a planar kinematic simulation, not a physical robot controller.

captions.title: 2 · Plan through configuration space
captions.text: A* searches pairs of joint angles. The planner checks both links and uses conservative swept-motion bounds to validate the route within the model.

captions.title: Watch the arm detour
captions.text: The tip is not the whole robot: both links must avoid obstacles. Learned predictions never approve a movement.

captions.title: 3 · Train an actual collision classifier
captions.text: 100 training examples; k = 5. On 800 separate test configurations: accuracy 95.5%, collision recall 15.6%, and 27 missed collisions. All labels come from simulated geometry.

captions.title: More examples. Still no guarantee.
captions.text: 1,500 training examples: accuracy 97.6%, recall 75.0%, and 8 missed collisions in this test. Inspect false negatives, not accuracy alone. This is synthetic evidence, not hardware validation.

captions.title: 4 · Predict, experiment, explain
captions.text: Challenges connect inverse kinematics, path planning, and model evaluation. A local notebook and CSV/JSON exports preserve experiment evidence.

captions.title: 5 · Local computation, verified offline
captions.text: The browser network is now disabled. The app has reloaded and trained again using cached files. No AI API keys, account, cloud inference, or hardware are required.

captions.title: Evidence and contribution disclosure
captions.text: AI assistants provided extensive implementation and testing. The student supplied project direction and robotics background. No learning-outcome study, award, peer review, or physical-robot test is claimed.
